rule: System test files in providers must not use the prefix '_system'; follow the naming conventions shown in existing system test files within the same folder.
trigger: new file created under providers/*/tests/system/ whose filename starts with 'test_' followed by a service name and ends with '_system.py'
rationale: Airflow's system-test discovery relies on file-name conventions; the '_system' suffix pattern does not exist in the codebase and would cause the file to be ignored or misclassified.

evidence.excerpt: there are no files with prefix '_system' for system tests

rule: When a provider hook supports Application Default Credentials (ADC) as a keyless fallback, the parameter docstring for the key-file arguments must explicitly state when ADC is used and when an explicit key is still required.
trigger: diff adds or modifies an auth method that conditionally skips key-file loading (e.g. 'if not gcp_key_path and not gcp_keyfile_dict') without updating the ':param gcp_key_path:' or ':param gcp_keyfile_dict:' docstring lines
rationale: Users configure provider hooks from the connection UI; if the docstring still describes the key file as mandatory, operators enabling ADC-based keyless auth have no documentation telling them it is now optional.

evidence.excerpt: update this parameter doc to explicitly mention the ADC fallback

rule: When a hook docstring adds or removes supported auth types, the corresponding RST connection-docs file (connections/<provider>.rst) must be updated in the same PR.
trigger: diff modifies the ':param auth_type:' docstring list in a hook but does not touch the matching providers/*/docs/connections/*.rst file
rationale: Users configuring connections via the UI consult the rendered RST docs, not the hook source; leaving the RST stale means the new auth options are invisible to operators.

evidence.excerpt: rendered Vault connection docs stale; users configuring the connection UI won't see the new ADC flow

rule: Boolean Airflow configuration values must be read with conf.getboolean() rather than conf.get(), to prevent string literals such as 'False' from being evaluated as truthy.
trigger: diff introduces conf.get("<section>", "<key>", fallback=...) where the config key is documented or used as a boolean elsewhere in the codebase
rationale: conf.get() always returns a string; the string 'False' is truthy in Python, so boolean config flags read with conf.get() silently enable features the operator intended to disable.

evidence.excerpt: string 'False' will still be truthy and incorrectly enable team/global lookup

rule: Use the same fallback value consistently for every conf.getboolean() call that reads the same configuration key within a single module.
trigger: diff adds two or more conf.get*() calls for the same (section, key) pair with different fallback= values in the same file
rationale: Mismatched fallbacks mean the feature behaves differently depending on which code path is exercised first, making behavior unpredictable when the key is absent from airflow.cfg.

evidence.excerpt: avoid mixing different fallbacks in different places

rule: MagicMock objects standing in for credential or authentication objects in unit tests must specify spec= or use autospec=True; bare MagicMock() fabricates arbitrary attributes and allows tests to pass even when the code reads a nonexistent field.
trigger: diff introduces MagicMock() (without spec or autospec) assigned to a variable whose name contains 'credential', 'cred', 'token', or 'auth'
rationale: Bare mocks invent any attribute access as a new Mock, so a test can stay green while production code silently reads the wrong field from a real credential object.

evidence.excerpt: bare MagicMock fabricates arbitrary attributes; test can still pass even if wrong field

rule: Provider package documentation links must use the canonical URL scheme https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-providers-<name>/; omitting '-providers-' produces broken links after publication.
trigger: diff adds an RST hyperlink to https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-<name>/ (missing '-providers-' segment)
rationale: The published docs site uses the providers-prefixed path; links without it resolve to 404 once the package is live.

evidence.excerpt: points to apache-airflow-ibm-mq rather than apache-airflow-providers-ibm-mq

rule: Each release version heading in a provider's changelog.rst must appear exactly once; duplicate version headings produce malformed rendered changelogs.
trigger: diff adds a version heading (e.g. '0.1.0' followed by a RST underline) that already exists earlier in the same changelog.rst file
rationale: Sphinx renders each top-level heading as a separate section; a duplicate creates two identically-named sections which confuse readers and may break cross-references.

evidence.excerpt: 0.1.0 appears twice; will render confusing/duplicated sections in published changelog

rule: A new provider package-name in provider.yaml must use the top-level vendor namespace (apache-airflow-providers-<vendor>) rather than a service-level sub-name, matching how the Amazon and Google providers consolidate all services under one package.
trigger: diff adds a provider.yaml with package-name: apache-airflow-providers-<vendor>-<service> where <vendor> could host multiple services
rationale: Service-specific package names prevent future hooks for the same vendor from joining the package without a rename; the Amazon and Google precedents show all services sharing one vendor package.

evidence.excerpt: in future folks might want to add more IBM hooks that are not just message queues

rule: A hook's conn_type must be vendor-namespaced (e.g. 'ibm_mq'), not a generic protocol category (e.g. 'mq'), to avoid collision with other providers in the same protocol family.
trigger: diff adds conn_type = "<generic_category>" in a hook class where the category name (mq, queue, stream, etc.) could apply to multiple vendors
rationale: Airflow's connection registry is global; a generic conn_type blocks future providers in the same category from using a natural name without collision.

evidence.excerpt: if a future Rabbit/ActiveMQ/Solace provider lands, they can't take a natural conn_type

rule: MessageQueueTrigger must be instantiated with the queue= keyword argument (full URI), not scheme=; passing a full URI to the scheme= parameter raises ValueError before the DAG parses.
trigger: diff instantiates MessageQueueTrigger(scheme="<uri>://...") instead of MessageQueueTrigger(queue="<uri>://...")
rationale: MessageQueueTrigger matches providers by comparing self.scheme == scheme; a full URI is never equal to the short scheme string, so the constructor raises ValueError immediately.

evidence.excerpt: raises ValueError('scheme is not recognized') before the DAG ever parses

rule: When iterating triggering_asset_events in a DAG task, items are AssetEvent ORM objects; access their payload via .extra, not by dict-key subscription (["payload"]), which raises TypeError.
trigger: diff accesses triggering_asset_events[...] items via square-bracket key lookup such as event["payload"] or event["key"]
rationale: triggering_asset_events yields AssetEvent ORM instances; dict-style access raises TypeError at runtime on every triggered run, breaking every DAG that copies the pattern.

evidence.excerpt: AssetEvent object is not subscriptable; raises TypeError before print runs

rule: @patch decorators in provider hook unit tests must target the fully-qualified symbol as actually imported inside the module under test; patching a symbol the module never imports creates a no-op and leaves the real dependency unpatched.
trigger: diff adds @patch("airflow.providers.<pkg>.hooks.<module>.<function>") where <function> does not appear in the import list or module body of the hook being tested
rationale: Python's patch resolves names at the point of use; if the hook never imports the patched name, the decorator silently does nothing and the test exercises the real external call.

evidence.excerpt: patch decorators are no-ops; tests aren't exercising the real connection/consume path

rule: Unit tests for async provider hooks must include at least one test that exercises the real loop body with only I/O primitives patched; fully patching the method under test (e.g. consume()) makes the test blind to control-flow bugs inside that method.
trigger: diff adds an async hook test that patches the top-level method under test (e.g. patch.object(hook, 'consume', side_effect=[...])) rather than patching lower-level I/O (e.g. ibmmq.Queue.get)
rationale: Patching the method wholesale bypasses the retry loop and stop_event logic; bugs in that loop are invisible to the test suite.

evidence.excerpt: stop_event reuse bug is invisible; real consume() body never runs

rule: New input-validation errors raised inside provider hooks must use native Python exceptions (ValueError, TypeError) rather than AirflowException, per the dev-list decision to decouple providers from core exception types.
trigger: diff adds 'raise AirflowException(...)' inside a provider hook method that is performing argument or state validation (e.g. checking a parameter range or type)
rationale: A dev-list decision directs providers to use Python/provider-native exceptions so that providers remain independent of airflow-core's exception hierarchy.

evidence.excerpt: directive is not to use AirflowException but instead use native Python/Provider-native exceptions
